heroText: Bissau is Guinea-Bissau's low-rise coastal capital, built around a Portuguese colonial core on the Geba River estuary. First-time visitors should walk the fading colonnades of Praca, browse produce and cloth at Bandim Market, and see the star-shaped ramparts of the Fortaleza d'Amura. Osvaldo Vieira International Airport is the practical starting point for exploring the wider Bijagos Archipelago just offshore.

areas.name: Praca
areas.text: Praca is Bissau's colonial centre, with the Presidential Palace, cathedral and faded Portuguese buildings, best for a first stay near government offices.

areas.name: Bissau Velho
areas.text: Bissau Velho, the old town by the port, holds the Fortaleza d'Amura and narrow colonial streets, good for walking and history.

areas.name: Bandim
areas.text: Bandim is home to the city's largest and busiest market, useful for produce, textiles and everyday city life rather than lodging.

airports.search: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport, Bissau, Guinea-Bissau
airports.text: Osvaldo Vieira International Airport sits just north of central Bissau; flight schedules are limited, so confirm connections and hotel transfers in advance.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Osvaldo Vieira International Airport (OXB) and central Bissau before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Praca for an easy first stay near the Presidential Palace and cathedral, or Bissau Velho for colonial streets and port views close to the Fortaleza d'Amura. Keep Bandim for daytime market visits rather than an overnight base.
hotelIntro: Bissau's small hotel scene centres on Praca and Bissau Velho, both close to the port, cathedral and colonial landmarks, with a handful of business-style hotels serving visitors heading onward to the Bijagos Archipelago.
rentalCars: A rental car is rarely useful in compact central Bissau; taxis cover the city, while trips to the Bijagos Archipelago require a boat rather than a car.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Praca or Bissau Velho for an easy first stay close to the cathedral, port and colonial-era landmarks.

travelTips.title: Flight planning
travelTips.text: Confirm international flight schedules well ahead, since Osvaldo Vieira International Airport has limited weekly connections to regional hubs.

travelTips.title: Cash
travelTips.text: Carry West African CFA francs in cash, since card acceptance is rare outside the largest hotels and offices.

travelTips.title: Bijagos planning
travelTips.text: Book Bijagos Archipelago boat transfers or lodges in advance from Bissau, since onward transport is infrequent and fills up quickly.

history.label: 16th century
history.text: When the Portuguese began to trade there in the 16th century, the king of Bissau was among the most supportive monarchs of the region.
In 1680 Bissau even helped the Portuguese in a conflict with the Papels of Cacheu.
The city was founded in 1687 as a Portuguese trading post.
In response the Portuguese Conselho Ultramarino established the captaincy-general of Bissau, and by 1696 the town had a fort, a church, and a hospital.
The fort was rebuilt by the Grão Pará and Maranhão Company in 1775 to better project Portuguese power and store more slaves for shipment to Brazil.
In 1869, as part of an effort to more efficiently govern the territory, Bissau was raised to the status of commune.

history.label: 20th century

In 1941 the capital was transferred from Bolama to Bissau.

After the declaration of independence by the anti-colonial guerrillas of PAIGC in 1973, the capital of the rebel territories was declared to be Madina do Boe, while Bissau remained the colonial capital.

history.text: According to oral tradition, the kingdom was founded by Mecau, the son of the king of Quinara (Guinala), who moved to the area with his pregnant sister, six wives, and subjects of his father's.
